target_customer: Hospitals, clinics, infusion suites and emergency and surgical units that want to improve patient flow and room use
problem: Clinics and hospitals lose capacity to waiting rooms and poorly scheduled workflows, and they lack measured data on where patients and staff spend time.
business_model: B2B hardware sensors and software subscription for hospital operations
product_category: Healthcare operations analytics with location sensors

founders.background_notes: Founder and CEO on the YC page. Background not found in opened sources.

founders.background_notes: Founder and CSO on the YC page. Background not found in opened sources.

competitors.traction_then: Deployed in hospitals; coverage describes AI over RTLS and clinical system data

competitors.name: Qventus
competitors.what: Machine learning software that optimizes real-time hospital operational decisions
competitors.funding_then: Series B announced May 2018, amount not confirmed in opened source

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining beacon hardware, location accuracy in hospitals, workflow analytics and simulation is standard IoT engineering with hospital integration hurdles.

defensibility.rationale: Hospital deployments and accumulated workflow data could lock in customers, but real-time location systems were an established category with funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented in sources found; no acquisition reported.

market_need_then: Hospital throughput and wait times were funded problems in 2018, shown by Tagnos raising 5 million dollars in March 2018 and Qventus raising a Series B in May 2018.

identity.voice_and_tone: Outcome claims such as eliminating the waiting room

branding.brand_signature: The goal statement to eliminate the waiting room

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, community or merch found; the name is generic health wording and the company has very little coverage.

outcome_analysis: Apprentice Health is listed as active and sells sensors and software to improve hospital efficiency, claiming 20 to 30 percent more exam room capacity and up to 50 percent shorter waits. Public information is very thin: no funding amounts, press, acquisition or shutdown was found, so its trajectory is unknown rather than poor.
